questions.answer: I really do. I love the challenge of finding something that suits the person perfectly, and their reaction when they open it is the best part. A [[thoughtful]] gift means far more than an expensive one.

questions.q: What was the last gift you bought for someone?
questions.answer: A set of picture books for my four-year-old nephew. He's at that age where he wants stories read to him constantly, so I chose ones with [[vivid]] illustrations. My sister says he takes them to bed every night.

Of course, who doesn't? But what I appreciate most is the thought behind it. A small, meaningful present from someone who knows me well means much more than something [[lavish]] given without much care.

questions.q: When do people give gifts in your country?
questions.answer: Mainly at Eid, weddings and birthdays, although birthdays are a more recent custom in many families. At weddings especially, gift-giving is quite an [[elaborate]] affair, and relatives sometimes feel pressure to give something impressive.

questions.q: Do you think it's better to give money or a gift?
questions.answer: It depends on the person. Money is practical, especially for newly married couples, and Eid salami is a much-loved custom. But a carefully chosen gift shows real [[consideration]], so for close friends I'd always choose something personal.
